To what point is the 'right' to be wrong acceptable? Traditionally, liberal ideology was structured around allowing dissenting opinions, no matter how 'contrary' they were to the widely-accepted popular beliefs. However as time goes on, it seems more as if the 'liberal' ideology has shifted towards 'tolerance', and through this 'tolerance' the standard has become to accept intolerant ideologies which are entirely contrary to classical 'liberal' values.

Is this just a standard shift in the paradigm?

Has this happened many times before?

Up until what point do you have the 'right' to be wrong?

Are all the proposed 'privileges' truly earned by being on the giving-end of a gun? And if so, is it always the provocateurs who gain the upper-hand of the arrangement, or is it those who plan the pre-arrangement? And to what extent is it required for one to understand the pre-arrangement before they are pre-selected to partake in the planned system of the future? And to what extent are you allowed to absorb these changes and redirect yourself?

Some of these things are very complicated to understand if you are 'out of the loop' and attempting to discover them on your own. Perhaps that is why there needs to be allowed a certain amount of time for young people and students to have the 'right' to be wrong; if only on a temporary basis.
